_why: Ratchet floors. A gate whose check count can fall silently cannot detect a deleted requirement: stripping four required headings from one pack made validate.py drop 1270->1269 and sloplint.py 224->223, both still green. Each number is the count measured on the commit named below. Raise freely; lowering one needs a reason in the same commit.
_measured_on: main, merge(feat/status-on-field) + feat(editorial-luxury), 2026-08-13, with a nested worktree present AND absent -- the two now agree
_raised: validate_palette.py 993 -> 1001: editorial-luxury's status set arrived in 1.25.0 from a concurrent run -- eight semantic colours, each measured against the field of its own theme by the check below. Additive with nothing else: 958 base + 8 theirs + 35 mine. validate.py holds at 2067, but the number means something it did not mean before: both ROOT markdown walks now skip nested checkouts, so the count no longer moves with whether a worktree happens to exist. It did move -- 2361 with one present against 2067 clean on the same commit, and 2361 was the number this file was about to enshrine. The plant for it is the only one whose pass condition is silence: a nested checkout must change neither verdict nor count. validate_palette.py 958 -> 993: validate_status_on_field() checks every semantic colour against the field of its own theme, which nothing did before -- validate_theme() computed one contrast, ink against field, and went straight to peer separation. On its first run it found 28 findings in 11 of 17 packs, and the worst was mechanical: scoreboard's [data-surface="panel"] block remapped eleven tokens and not the status set, so var(--good) painted 3.69:1 on the dark band while --good-on-dark had 10.21 three lines away. Two plants, one per tier. validate.py and sloplint.py are unchanged at 2066 and 450. validate.py 2066 -> 2067: SURFACE_COMPOSITION.md documents the new role marker, which adds one relative-link check.
